purpose: Target water profile catalog for beer recipe design with BJCP-aware defaults, modern brewery/author references, searchable aliases in English/Russian, and explicit separation between reusable water targets and beer styles.
design_notes: Profiles and styles are intentionally separated. A BJCP style is not the same thing as a water profile; styles map to default and alternate target profiles.
The mapping layer solves the Brewfather-like duplication problem more cleanly: styles remain reference data, while water profiles remain reusable numeric targets.
This file includes 128 BJCP 2021 style/substyle mapping entries: 125 leaf styles plus 3 umbrella entries (7C Kellerbier, 21B Specialty IPA, 27A Historical Beer).
Two contextual defaults are included for specialty categories where a fixed numeric target would be misleading; the app should derive water from the declared base style in those cases.
Search should index both profiles.aliases and bjcp_style_defaults.search_aliases so queries like 'ipa', 'бланш', 'дуббель', or 'кёльш' surface the correct profiles.
For Hazy IPA and other modern hop-forward beers, multiple brewery/author references are preserved as alternates rather than forcing a single 'correct' profile.
v3 adds explicit quick-pick navigation for high-frequency profile selection in the water profile picker.
Target profiles remain separate from BJCP styles. Styles map to defaults and alternatives; profiles are reusable across many styles.
Historical city profiles are intentionally preserved as references but should not dominate the default picker view.

separate_tabs_recommendation.why: Styles describe the beer; profiles describe the target water. They should be connected by mapping, not merged into one duplicated list.
separate_tabs_recommendation.default_ui_behavior: When the user selects a BJCP style, automatically suggest the mapped default profile and show alternates inline with source labels.

search_recommendation.notes: Profile search should match family terms as well as exact names; searching 'ipa' should surface all IPA defaults and source-specific alternates.
